EDA IBM HR Analytics Project¶

Project Title¶

Employee attrition analysis using pandas,numpay,matplot and seaborn¶

Introduction¶

Employee attrition is one of the biggest challenges faced by organizations because losing skilled employees increases recruitment costs and reduces productivity this project analyzes the IBM HR analytics dataset to identify the key factors influencing employee attrition .using python for data cleaning and exploratory data analysis (EDA) sql for business queries, and Power BI for dashboard visualization, the project provides actionable insights that can help the HR department improve employee retention and make data-driven decisions.

Objective¶

Analyze employee attrition patterns. Identify factors affecting employee satisfaction. Compare salary across departments. Understand overtime impact on attrition. Generate business insights for HR decision-making.

The employees were categorized into four age groups: Young Adults (18–30), Adults (31–40), Middle-Aged Adults (41–50), and Senior Adults (51–60). This classification provides a better understanding of the workforce distribution across different career stages. It helps identify the dominant age group within the organization and supports HR in workforce planning, talent management, and future recruitment strategies. Such segmentation also makes demographic analysis easier and more meaningful.

In [193]:
sns.countplot(x='Attrition', data=df)
plt.title('Employee attrition count')
plt.show()

The count plot shows that most employees have not left the organization, while a smaller number of employees have left the company. This indicates a relatively low attrition rate and suggests that the organization has good employee retention. However, analyzing the reasons for employee attrition can help HR further improve retention policies.

In [195]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.histplot(df['Age'], bins=20)
plt.title('Employee age Distribution')
plt.show()

The age distribution indicates that the majority of employees fall within the 25–40 years age range. This suggests that the organization primarily consists of young and mid-career professionals who are in their most productive working years. The presence of a strong workforce in this age group reflects a balanced employee base with potential for long-term growth and career development.

In [196]:
plt.figure(figsize=(6,8))
sns.countplot(x='Department',hue='Attrition',data=df)
plt.title("Department wise Atrrition")
plt.show()

The department-wise attrition analysis shows that the Research & Development department has the highest number of employees who have not left the organization, indicating strong employee retention in this department. In contrast, the HR department has the lowest number of employees who left the company. These findings suggest that employee retention varies across departments and can help HR identify areas that may require targeted retention strategies.

In [ ]:
In [198]:
plt.figure(figsize=(8,5))
sns.boxplot( x='Attrition',y='MonthlyIncome', data=df)
plt.title('Monthly Income vs Attrition')
plt.show()

The box plot compares the monthly income distribution of employees based on attrition status. The "No" category contains a larger number of employees than the "Yes" category, indicating that most employees have remained with the organization. While employees who left are fewer in number, the salary ranges of both groups overlap, suggesting that monthly income alone may not be the only factor influencing employee attrition.

In [199]:
plt.figure(figsize=(10,5))
sns.countplot(y='JobRole', hue='Attrition',data=df)
plt.title('Job Role Wise atrrition')
plt.show()

The job role-wise attrition analysis shows that Sales Executives have the highest number of employees who have not left the organization, while the Human Resources role has the lowest number of employees in the "No" category. Among employees who left the organization, Laboratory Technicians have the highest attrition count, whereas Research Directors have the lowest. These findings indicate that employee retention and attrition vary across job roles and can help HR identify roles that may require targeted retention strategies.

In [200]:
sns.histplot(df['MonthlyIncome'],bins=30)
plt.title('Monthly income Distribution')
plt.show()

The monthly income distribution shows that most employees earn between 2,500 and 15,000. The distribution is concentrated in the lower and middle income ranges, while comparatively fewer employees receive higher salaries. This indicates that the organization has a larger workforce in entry-level and mid-level positions, with a smaller proportion of high-income employees.

Employees who travel rarely make up the largest workforce and therefore account for the highest number of attrition cases. However, employees who travel frequently also show a relatively higher attrition trend compared to non-travel employees, suggesting that business travel may influence employee retention

In [207]:
sns.countplot(x='TrainingTimesLastYear',hue='Attrition',data =df)

plt.show()

Employees who received 2–3 trainings formed the largest workforce and also showed the highest retention. Employees with higher training exposure (4–6 trainings) had relatively lower attrition, suggesting that continuous learning and development programs may help improve employee retention.”

One-line recommendation¶

Company ko regular learning & development (L&D) programs continue rakhne chahiye aur 0–1 training wale employees par special focus karna chahiye taaki engagement aur retention improve ho sake.

Overall Business Recommendations (IBM HR Analytics Project)¶

Based on the complete analysis of Education Field, Gender, Business Travel, Training, Years at Company, Work-Life Balance, and Monthly Income, the company should consider the following actions:

1. Reduce Early Employee Attrition¶

Focus on employees in their first 1–5 years. Improve onboarding, mentoring, and career development programs. Conduct regular one-on-one meetings with new employees.

2. Strengthen Learning & Development¶

Provide 2–4 quality training sessions every year. Offer role-specific technical and soft-skill training. Create clear learning and career growth paths.

3. Improve Work-Life Balance¶

Introduce flexible work schedules where possible. Monitor employee workload to avoid burnout. Expand wellness and mental health initiatives.

4. Optimize Business Travel¶

Reduce unnecessary travel by using virtual meetings. Provide better travel allowances and recovery time for frequent travelers. Regularly review travel policies based on employee feedback.

5. Improve Employee Retention¶

Conduct stay interviews with high-performing employees. Recognize employee achievements through rewards and appreciation. Build transparent promotion and career progression policies.

6. Salary & Career Growth¶

Review salary structure regularly to ensure market competitiveness. Provide performance-based increments and promotions. Maintain transparent compensation policies.

7. Data-Driven HR Decisions¶

Track monthly attrition, promotions, training completion, and employee satisfaction using HR dashboards. Identify high-risk employees using predictive analytics and intervene early.

8. Recruitment Strategy¶

Continue hiring qualified candidates from strong educational backgrounds. Maintain diversity in hiring while ensuring the right skills for business n

Overall Conclusion¶

The analysis indicates that the company has strong overall employee retention, as the number of employees staying with the organization is significantly higher than those leaving.¶

However, the analysis also highlights several areas that require attention:¶

Attrition is highest among employees in their early years with the company.¶

Employees with poor work-life balance and frequent business travel may require additional support.¶

Continuous training and career development appear to contribute positively to employee retention.¶

Monthly income generally increases with age and experience, reflecting career progression within the organization.¶

The workforce is primarily composed of employees from Life Sciences and Medical backgrounds, indicating the company's focus on technical and scientific talent.¶

Overall, the company should focus on employee engagement, learning & development, work-life balance, competitive compensation, and data-driven HR strategies. Implementing these initiatives can help reduce attrition, improve employee satisfaction, and enhance long-term organizational performance.¶
